findings.title: Document the actual SLA __typename values
findings.failure: The tool description advertises literal values such as Pending and Breaching, but responses contain ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending and ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailBreaching. MCP consumers comparing against the documented values will fail to recognize SLA states.
findings.fix: Explain that __typename contains the ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail prefix, and give an exact returned value.
findings.evidence: packages/core-graphql/src/resolvers.ts:11918 returns the full concrete type names for all six statuses. GraphQL.js src/type/introspection.ts, TypeNameMetaFieldDef.resolve, returns parentType.name; it does not shorten the name.

findings.title: Reuse an SLA detail fragment within each operation
findings.failure: The PR introduces twelve identical status-detail selections. Future timestamp or status changes require twelve coordinated edits, allowing the four SLA targets to return inconsistent detail shapes.
findings.fix: Define an operation-local fragment on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail in each file and spread it into all four targets.
findings.evidence: A local token comparison confirmed all twelve selections are identical. lambdas/core-graphql-api/src/threads/changeThreadPriorityMutation.slas.litest.ts:36 already uses fragment slaFields on this union; services/mcp-server/operations/getBroadcastDetails.graphql:122 demonstrates operation-local fragment reuse in MCP operations.

checked_fine: Deploy: Dockerfile copies the changed operations into the ECS image, and mcp.config.yaml loads that directory. All selected fields and filter types already exist in HEAD~1; no new schema deployment dependency, environment variable, secret, permission, resource, or export is introduced.

Contract: Token comparison against HEAD~1 confirmed every existing query field, argument, default, sort, and pagination selection is preserved in all three files. The new filters are optional and default to null.
Contract: All six SLA union variants select valid timestamp fields, including pause details for Pending and ImminentBreach. The existing resolver adds no permission requirement.
Data: The changes only extend read operations; no writes, migrations, deletion policies, or retention changes.

Silent regression: The all-null SLA filter returns an empty SQL fragment in threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943. Historical tracker matching is explicitly documented, and the summary uses the existing latest-tracker resolver.
Silent regression: Threads without a tier or SLA policy return four null targets without loading trackers; other threads use the existing batched, traced dataloader.
Operability: Operation edits remain inside the Docker asset build context, so they participate in image redeployment.
Rollback: HEAD~1 supports the same backend schema. Rolling back removes the new MCP fields and filters without leaving incompatible stored data or infrastructure.
Blast radius: No shared constants, helpers, schemas, or lists change; the additions affect these three MCP tools.

Dead code: Searches across services, packages, lambdas, testing, test, infra, terraform, and docs traced operation loading and SLA consumers. Both added variables are referenced, and the union resolver produces every selected branch.
Validation scope: Review and token comparisons were local and read-only. Runtime tests were not run; node_modules is absent.
